text: Ravens fans, I'm excited to sit down with team president Sashi Brown here at the NFL owners meetings. Sashi, thank you so much for the time. >> Good to be with you. When you look at the big picture of the organization, what do you see as the top organizational priorities right now? >> Winning. >> Always number one. >> Winning is always number one. Uh, and we got to get back on top of this division and protect Lamar, run the ball, play solid defense on the field, which, uh, I'm confident we will do. Uh, and then I think the second thing is just to stay relentless about, you know, our fan experience, our game day experience and our fan engagement overall. That's really the the second most important thing that we can do. There's a lot of technology coming. Our stadium renovations are really exciting. We're going to roll out the third phase of those which we're we're super excited about here uh you know in the next several months. And so I think just all of those opportunities, a new coaching staff here that's going to be exciting uh with the team that's really compete for championships. So it's an exciting time to be the Ravens to be I think in the in the flock the fan base of the Ravens. Um and now we just need to continue to capitalize and continue to push ourselves towards championship on the field. Uh and then in the stadium as well. >> Well, you mentioned the stadium. That has been a major project that has been ongoing here for for the last few years and and like you said, this year we get to kind of put a bow on it and unveil all these great new spaces that are going to come to completion. What has you most excited about the completion of this project and what it's going to mean for our stadium? >> I think the transformation and the unveiling of the new stadium in amalgamation of all the projects. So, you know, we added some premium which is important, but the majority of what we've done and invested in has been the GA experience. The every fan that comes in the stadium is going to have a bunch of new spaces and opportunities to engage and activate with their friends with us uh around the stadium, whether that's upper concourse and some of the things that you'll see rolled out there with the bump out of thousands of new square footage. um you know, protection from precipitation and cold, uh more bathrooms, cut those lines down, new points of sale, uh concessions so people aren't standing in line, they can get back to their seats. But then a plaza, right, that brings all of that traditional Baltimore tailgate activity and energy on game day uh into our plaza and get that connectivity, that energy going really early. Uh we're really excited about technology that's going to really be interlaid throughout the entire stadium uh to give people a more dynamic experience uh and be able to sound and and mostly uh visual opportunity to stay connected to the game uh when you are in the concourses outside of your seats. So, you know, it's been a a long project, as you said, a lot of great planning from our staff and and I want to shout out Rich Tamayo and Brad DS and a bunch of others that have put in just an extraordinary amount of effort. And and I'd be remiss if I didn't uh thank the folks down in Annapolis for the trust that they put into us uh to to renovate the stadium along with the Maryland Stadium Authority and our partnership there. Something that stands out to me is of course there's Ravens game day and you just talked through that and that's going to be just just changing in such a big way for our game day experience. But all of these renovations have also helped open up the stadium beyond Sundays and Mondays for Ravens football on Thursdays but throughout the entire year. We just had the DC United Inner Miami game with Messi in Baltimore Morgan Wallen concerts this summer. We have the All Blacks for South Africa game coming up this fall. So, you have all these major events that are coming to Baltimore. What What does it mean to have a list of events coming to our city and our stadium? >> You know, as one of the objectives, we tend to not pat ourselves on the back, pound our our chest too much, but it is not uncommon when we go to meet opposing ownership and greet them down on the field pregame that they really are complimentary of just the bones and the way that we've kept up MNT Bank Stadium. again partnership with the Stadium Authority of Maryland, the state and and the Ravens. Steve's been very generous allowing us to invest uh upwards of $300 million into the stadium beyond what we're required to do under the the uh lease with with the state. So, we've been forward investors and I think it shows. So, the stadium's in in great shape. Then you get an opportunity to say, okay, with the state, how do we reinvest to make sure that MNT Bank Stadium and the Orioles are doing the same at uh Oral Park, how do we make sure that our stadium maintains its status as one of the best in the league? And with the bones in place and upwards of $400 plus million dollars of investment, we have maintained, I think, the integrity of the design and the feel and the culture of Mnt Bank Stadium while really adding some fantastic proven uh opportunities for fans to engage and watch the game in different ways from different places being greater proximity, but also just to bring more of a game day experience and a festive kind of atmosphere to the stadium. So, we're really excited about all that. I think at the end of the day, uh, what that means is we can go out to promoters who are looking to bring iconic global events like All Blacks versus South Africa, uh, to a stadium like ours because when they come in and they see things that they just haven't seen in another environment, we're still one of the few outdoor stadiums that has all the the premium opportunities, but then the technology and engaged and fan activation areas uh, that are at the forefront of what the stadium experience is today. It's allowed us to bring more and more events and we're excited. A historic number, six nights this year of non-Ravens events to the stadium. We're going to continue to try to pursue and sustain if not grow that moving forward. Uh and the renovations were a huge piece of that um and the vision around that. And that's what we talked to Governor Hogan, Governor Moore, and their administrations about. That's really important for us to deliver to Mayor Scott uh more events, major events, bowl events to downtown Baltimore. >> It's exciting. It's going to be a lot of fun events there. Another important piece of of news here coming out of the owners meetings was the BV1 vote uh which allowed the Ravens to now market in the territories uh south of us Prince George's County and Montgomery County. Uh and this has been an ongoing conversation uh but it passed here at league meetings. What's the significance of this and and what does this mean for the Ravens? >> Let me start with a little history if that's okay. So, you know, when the NFL constitution and bylaws were passed, there was always a diving of rights. What could the leagues do? What could the clubs do? Visa v the league, visa v each other. And BV1 is the provision that largely govern the rights between the clubs and the leagues. There was a special provision in BV1 for any teams that were in really close proximity to each other to say, okay, this is how we're going to divvy up the rights. That's probably a little bit of a regressive uh way of thinking about the world now that we have the internet and social media and all these different things. The way we engage with fans, fanhood is no longer so geographic. Uh BV1 expired on its natural terms or was set to expire tomorrow. Today we had a vote to extend but also evolve BV1. And one of the places we wanted to take as a league a close look was how do two stadiums that are 30 mi apart really think about the territory that lies in between them. And I think we got to a good point with Montgomery and PG County that are in really close proximity both less than 20 mi from our stadium whereas before we were restricted in certain ways from being able to activate in those areas. So when we looked at it with the league and the entire body of ownership uh the thought was to evolve it. Now that we're we're sharing those markets uh in Montgomery County and PG County, we're excited about that. We have hundreds of thousands of Ravens fans uh across uh Montgomery, PG County, and of course, Northern Virginia and DC, just as the Commanders have uh a number of fans in the the Baltimore territory, so to speak. But this was a good uh landing spot for us to evolve and to be able to activate uh both uh with with fans and allow some of our partners to activate in those two counties, important counties to us and where we have a ton of members of the flock. >> Yeah, no doubt. Something that will be re relevant in those counties and also in Baltimore is the continued work that we do in the community. This past year we had some major legacy projects that we rolled out the Hilton Rec Center uh which was really big. just most recently a few weeks ago partnering with College Track to open the Baltimore Ravens College Track Center in Baltimore. These are these are major projects that are going to have a big impact on the community. It's really part of, I think, their faith and their belief system and they want the organization to reflect that. So, when you look at our mission, it's right there. win games, amaze our fans, impact the community in a positive way. You asked earlier, uh, you know, what's most important for us to focus on, and I said winning and fans. Uh, but in line with that, you know, one of the things that I think I'm most proud of here is to with our entire staff really dive in in a serious deep way, uh, in a rich way how we impact the community in some of our community work. And Steve really challenged us. He said, "You know, you all do a lot high volume of events. Can we find some things that will have legacy deep impact and you talked about our two, you know, kind of crown jewel projects. One in the Hilton Community Center, uh, with Boys and Girls Club, the Ravens Boys and Girls Club, uh, which is going to be a fantastic and already is, but is going to continue to be a fantastic for decades space for kids after school in the that community in West Baltimore. And then the second is our Ravens college access program which is a $50 million commitment over 10 years bridges collegebound now the Baltimore Ravens college track facility which we just opened a couple weeks ago touching thousands of kids uh across Baltimore and helping them find their way to prepare to go to college, get into school and then um you know be successful once you get into school. Most of these kids are firstgen students and we have made it extraordinarily uh difficult to navigate getting into college, having success college and then getting out, you know, with with great jobs. And all three of these programs and their leadership uh are proven, have great track records, uh and it's a way for us to give back to youth and education. And we feel like education's tremendously transformative and we're huge believers in the youth of our city. I want to bring it back to the field for a minute. You mentioned the coaching staff. It's not just Jesse and that's been the big focus, but there's it's all new coaches. We see it every day in the building. You're getting to know uh people who are coming to the building for the first time and it's it's been a massive change. >> How is that? We feel the energy, you know, and seeing it every day that it's just it's it's people who are coming in and looking to build something and there's just this energy and excitement. How have you seen uh the energy factor with this new coaching staff? Yeah, they're they're to a to a coach really positive, engaging, really bringing fresh ideas, working well together. I I'm really excited when the players get back uh to see the interaction between the staff and and some of our players and the leadership in particular and how they ingrained. But Jess is available. Uh he's they're they're present and uh it's been a as you said just a lift in the building. really refreshing to have uh some young energy and new ideas around. Uh and that's with all due respect obviously to a tremendous staff that was here before. Uh but we're really excited about what uh what is to come and we'll start to see it roll out this spring in a couple weeks. >> No doubt. You one new hire that you made this year connected to coaching but a little bit different is Dr. Nick Gil who's going to be over uh the entire performance operation. I'm curious what went into that hire, how did that come about? How did he come on your radar and and ultimately uh what made this decision to bring him in and oversee that unit? >> Yeah, both both Eric and I for some time uh have looked around sport uh and noticed some things that we saw, learned uh and and exposed ourselves to best practices in global sport. And there are some places where I think we've we've both felt like we could get better on the performance side of medical. Traditionally, those two um functions sit on different sides of the building, report differently. And you know, there's a high performance model that we've seen elsewhere that we're going to in integrate here. And Nick is a guy who's been really successful for a long period of time was looking for a challenge. Uh I had been in contact with him and some others, you know, at the uh elite level of of high performance models combining medical and performance. Uh Eric had some folks that he understood and we went through an interview process and we're really uh impressed with Nick and we're excited about what he'll bring to the table to help us get better every day. And uh I think he's going to help us tremendously. I'm really excited to get him here in the building in I think just a couple days. >> Yeah. Well, him and the players are coming back and and the last one, as you mentioned, the players are going to be back. We're all we all feel that energy and the excitement when they're in the building and and you talked about Jesse and the the expectations as players come back and you look at this season, you look at the steps leading into this year. >> What are the expectations, you know, for this season uh with a new head coach and and the championship aspirations that that exist? Uh but as everyone comes back into the building, you look ahead to the season, what are the expectations? >> Still still blood in the mouth from Pittsburgh. uh you know, so so absolutely eager to get back uh onto the field and and chase another Super Bowl this year. Uh I know to a to a player in that locker room, everyone feels like uh they're ready to to get back after it. And uh we left with that bad taste of your mouth, which you normally do, but that one was particularly tough to take. So I know guys want to turn that back around and they're going to be eager to learn the new system and get get after it. Uh, I would say, you know, from my perspective as I look at the 2026 season, I mean, we don't want to put too much pressure on Jess, but we've got a MVP caliber, uh, quarterback, star-studded defense, and we've added a guy like Trey, you know, to our pass rush. We think that's going to help us. Uh, we've got a couple picks here high that we're eager to deploy and bring some folks in that can help us as well. You know, how well we've coached and developed. That's going to be a hallmark of what we do continually. So, uh, we're not lowering our standards. At the same time, we're going to be realistic about it, but really excited to see Declan and Jesse get to work crafting this defense with Weave. Uh, so it's going to be exciting, exciting spring, and I know the players are eager to get going. Well, >> we can't wait. Sashi, appreciate the time. Thank you so much. >> Always. Thanks, G. >> Thank you.

title: Ed Policy 1-on-1: Packers 'one-of-one' amongst NFL teams
text: Hey everybody, Packers president and CEO Ed Policy joined us from the league meetings and Ed, as I understand it, growing up, you came to these things. What's it like to return as the Packers president and CEO? Uh thanks, Larry. Well, first off, uh it's great to be with you down here in Arizona. And yeah, I've been coming to these for quite some time. I think my first one was actually at this very resort. I remember when I was about 11 years old, my father was working for the 49ers back then. I was kind of shushed away from the pool because my father and Bill Walsh were in a heated discussion using some language that I think my mother didn't want me to hear. You have your football leadership, Brian, Matt, and Russ in place for the foreseeable future. Is that a comforting thought as you move forward? Yeah, it sure is. I I couldn't be happier and I couldn't be more confident about the three people that we have in place. You know, I I've known Russ Ball for over 25 years. I think he and I worked together with the Arena Football League. I've worked with Brian now for 14 years and and was part of bringing Matt in 7 years ago. So, I couldn't be more confident in them. Uh really excited about the future with all three of those guys. I've seen where building on and maintaining your presence in the league is one of your priorities. Is that already happening? It it is and you know, things like these annual meetings are critical to really build that. I would say uh you know, by way of example, I now sit on many of the business and policy setting committees that the league has and uh I'm really excited because for the first time our head coach sits on the head coaches sub advisory committee and our GM sits on the uh GMAC, which is the GM advisory committee. So, I think the Packers have more of a voice than ever at these meetings. Now, you were part of a number of votes this morning. Anything out of that that you would consider the headline act? You know, maybe the headline is that it's nowhere near as dramatic as it was last year, if you remember. We had a lot of discussion about the tush push and I'm glad that we're not talking about that this year. I think there's an interesting tweak to the new kickoff rule. Now, any team can declare an onside kick at any point in the game. Last year, [music] it was just uh you had to be the losing team and it had to be in the fourth quarter. During your informal session with the local media guys yesterday, you made a point of saying and emphasizing the fact that Packers are in great shape right now, but you have to approach things, and I love the phrase, with a healthy paranoia. Could you elaborate a little bit? >> Sure. Well, yeah, you know, it starts with recognizing the fact that the Packers are an extreme anomaly. We're one of one, there's nothing else like us given our our unique ownership structure and we do have to compete with the rest of the the other 31 teams in the NFL and they have access to money and capital that the Packers don't have in a few forms. Obviously, they're owned by very wealthy owners and a few, you know, more recent dynamics, they have access to private equity money and not just private equity, but just more limited partners buying minority interest in their team. So, any other team now can raise hundreds of millions of dollars by simply selling non-controlling limited partnerships in their team and and again, giving up equity, but certainly not giving up any control. You've also seen an increase in the the amount of public money being invested in the stadiums across the country and in and other markets, we don't have access to that right now. So, with all of that, the fact that we've got to have got to have a really successful business off the field to be able to compete on the field with all those other teams, we [music] just have to be really smart, really forward-looking, and um on top of some of these trends. Ed, moving forward, is there a biggest challenge on the horizon for the Green Bay Packers? Yeah, I I would say it's um competition. The NFL [music] has never been more competitive both on and off the field. You saw the games last year were closer than they've ever been. It feels like so many of the teams are just kind of bunched together. The parity's never been better than it is. I think the championship belongs to anybody next year, which means it belongs to us. We've just got to reach out and take it. Touchdown, Green Bay Packers!
